references.authors: Ye L, Dinkova-Kostova AT, Wade KL, et al.
references.title: Quantitative determination of dithiocarbamates in human plasma, serum, erythrocytes and urine: pharmacokinetics of broccoli sprout isothiocyanates in humans
references.finding: After ~200 µmol broccoli-sprout isothiocyanates, plasma levels peaked at about 1 h (0.9-2.3 µM) and fell with a half-life of 1.77 h; 58% of the dose was in urine by 8 h.

references.authors: Vermeulen M, Klöpping-Ketelaars IW, van den Berg R, et al.
references.title: Bioavailability and kinetics of sulforaphane in humans after consumption of cooked versus raw broccoli
references.finding: Raw broccoli gave 37% sulforaphane bioavailability with a plasma peak at 1.6 h; cooked broccoli gave 3.4% with a peak at 6 h; excretion half-lives were 2.4-2.6 h.

references.authors: Shapiro TA, Fahey JW, Wade KL, et al.
references.title: Chemoprotective glucosinolates and isothiocyanates of broccoli sprouts: metabolism and excretion in humans
references.finding: Isothiocyanate excretion was linear from 25 to 200 µmol and varied only 9% across four repeated 50 µmol doses; chewing raised excretion vs swallowing whole.

references.authors: Egner PA, Chen JG, Wang JB, et al.
references.title: Bioavailability of Sulforaphane from two broccoli sprout beverages: results of a short-term, cross-over clinical trial in Qidong, China
references.finding: A sulforaphane-rich beverage gave ~70% bioavailability as a bolus; a glucoraphanin-rich beverage gave ~5% with slower elimination that approached steady-state exposure.

references.authors: Egner PA, Chen JG, Zarth AT, et al.
references.title: Rapid and sustainable detoxication of airborne pollutants by broccoli sprout beverage: results of a randomized clinical trial in China
references.finding: Daily broccoli sprout beverage (600 µmol glucoraphanin + 40 µmol sulforaphane) raised benzene mercapturic acid excretion 61% from day 1, sustained for 12 weeks; bioavailability did not decline.

references.authors: Chen JG, Johnson J, Egner P, et al.
references.title: Dose-dependent detoxication of the airborne pollutant benzene in a randomized trial of broccoli sprout beverage in Qidong, China
references.finding: Over 10 days, only the full-dose beverage (~25 µmol/day urinary sulforaphane metabolites) raised benzene detoxication (+63%); half and one-fifth doses did not.

references.authors: Kensler TW, Ng D, Carmella SG, et al.
references.title: Modulation of the metabolism of airborne pollutants by glucoraphanin-rich and sulforaphane-rich broccoli sprout beverages in Qidong, China
references.finding: Seven days of sulforaphane- or glucoraphanin-rich beverage raised pollutant mercapturic acids 20-50%; after a 5-day washout, biomarkers were back to pre-treatment levels (no carryover).

references.authors: Kensler TW, Chen JG, Egner PA, et al.
references.title: Effects of glucosinolate-rich broccoli sprouts on urinary levels of aflatoxin-DNA adducts and phenanthrene tetraols in a randomized clinical trial in He Zuo township, Qidong, People's Republic of China
references.finding: Nightly glucoraphanin infusion for 2 weeks did not change aflatoxin-DNA adducts overall, but people who excreted more sulforaphane metabolites had fewer adducts.

references.authors: Riedl MA, Saxon A, Diaz-Sanchez D
references.title: Oral sulforaphane increases Phase II antioxidant enzymes in the human upper airway
references.finding: Broccoli sprout homogenate once daily for 3 days raised nasal-cell NQO1, HO-1, GSTM1 and GSTP1 mRNA dose-dependently (about 2-3-fold at 200 g); alfalfa sprouts did nothing.

references.authors: Heber D, Li Z, Garcia-Lloret M, et al.
references.title: Sulforaphane-rich broccoli sprout extract attenuates nasal allergic response to diesel exhaust particles
references.finding: Four days of 100 µmol/day sulforaphane cut the nasal white-cell response to a diesel exhaust particle challenge by 54%.

references.authors: Atwell LL, Hsu A, Wong CP, et al.
references.title: Absorption and chemopreventive targets of sulforaphane in humans following consumption of broccoli sprouts or a myrosinase-treated broccoli sprout extract
references.finding: 200 µmol/day as one dose or two 100 µmol doses 12 h apart: split dosing kept plasma levels higher later in the day, but HO-1, HDAC activity and p21 in blood cells showed no dose response.

references.authors: Dinkova-Kostova AT, Fahey JW, Wade KL, et al.
references.title: Induction of the phase 2 response in mouse and human skin by sulforaphane-containing broccoli sprout extracts
references.finding: Topical sulforaphane raised human skin NQO1 activity 1.5-fold after one dose and 4.5-fold after three doses 24 h apart, showing that induced enzyme carries over and stacks between daily doses.

references.authors: Talalay P, Fahey JW, Healy ZR, et al.
references.title: Sulforaphane mobilizes cellular defenses that protect skin against damage by UV radiation
references.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
references.finding: Three daily topical sulforaphane doses cut UV erythema by 37.7%; in one subject protection was 32% at 48 h and 10% at 72 h after the last dose, attributed to long-lived induced proteins.

references.authors: Gao X, Dinkova-Kostova AT, Talalay P
references.title: Powerful and prolonged protection of human retinal pigment epithelial cells, keratinocytes, and mouse leukemia cells against oxidative damage: the indirect antioxidant effects of sulforaphane
references.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
references.finding: In human cells, a 24 h sulforaphane exposure gave protection against oxidants that kept rising for 24-48 h after removal and returned to control levels over the following days, tracking NQO1 and glutathione.

references.authors: Siegel D, Anwar A, Winski SL, et al.
references.title: Rapid polyubiquitination and proteasomal degradation of a mutant form of NAD(P)H:quinone oxidoreductase 1
references.finding: Wild-type NQO1 protein had a half-life over 18 h in cells (the common NQO1*2 variant was degraded in 1.2 h).

references.authors: Kobayashi A, Kang MI, Okawa H, et al.
references.title: Oxidative stress sensor Keap1 functions as an adaptor for Cul3-based E3 ligase to regulate proteasomal degradation of Nrf2
references.finding: Nrf2 protein has a half-life under 20 minutes because KEAP1 targets it for proteasomal degradation.

references.authors: Lee OH, Jain AK, Papusha V, et al.
references.title: An auto-regulatory loop between stress sensors INrf2 and Nrf2 controls their cellular abundance
references.finding: Nrf2 induces transcription of its own inhibitor KEAP1, a negative feedback loop that limits the size and duration of the response.

references.authors: Wakabayashi N, Itoh K, Wakabayashi J, et al.
references.title: Keap1-null mutation leads to postnatal lethality due to constitutive Nrf2 activation
references.finding: Mice lacking KEAP1, with permanently active Nrf2, died after birth from hyperkeratosis of the esophagus and forestomach.

references.authors: Xu Z, Wang S, Ji H, et al.
references.title: Broccoli sprout extract prevents diabetic cardiomyopathy via Nrf2 activation in db/db T2DM mice
references.finding: Broccoli sprout extract or sulforaphane by gavage every other day for 3 months prevented diabetic cardiomyopathy in mice via Nrf2.

references.authors: Myzak MC, Tong P, Dashwood WM, et al.
references.title: Sulforaphane retards the growth of human PC-3 xenografts and inhibits HDAC activity in human subjects
references.finding: A single 68 g serving of broccoli sprouts inhibited HDAC activity in human blood cells at 3 and 6 h.

references.authors: Sedlak TW, Nucifora LG, Koga M, et al.
references.title: Sulforaphane Augments Glutathione and Influences Brain Metabolites in Human Subjects: A Clinical Pilot Study
references.finding: Seven days of daily oral sulforaphane raised blood glutathione in healthy volunteers.

references.authors: Doss JF, Jonassaint JC, Garrett ME, et al.
references.title: Phase 1 Study of a Sulforaphane-Containing Broccoli Sprout Homogenate for Sickle Cell Disease
references.finding: Escalating broccoli sprout homogenate raised whole-blood HMOX1 mRNA on the last day of treatment.

references.authors: Bauman JE, Zang Y, Sen M, et al.
references.title: Prevention of Carcinogen-Induced Oral Cancer by Sulforaphane
references.finding: Sulforaphane induced NQO1 and GCLC in mucosal cells; in a pilot, buccal NQO1 mRNA rose 2-fold or more in 3-6 of 6-9 people depending on beverage.

references.authors: Ribeiro M, Alvarenga L, Coutinho-Wolino KS, et al.
references.title: Sulforaphane upregulates the mRNA expression of NRF2 and NQO1 in non-dialysis patients with chronic kidney disease
references.finding: 400 µg/day sulforaphane for 1 month raised blood NRF2 and NQO1 mRNA.

references.authors: Singh K, Connors SL, Macklin EA, et al.
references.title: Sulforaphane treatment of autism spectrum disorder (ASD)
references.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
references.finding: 50-150 µmol/day sulforaphane for 18 weeks improved behaviour scores; during 4 weeks off treatment scores rose back toward baseline.

references.authors: Yanaka A, Fahey JW, Fukumoto A, et al.
references.title: Dietary sulforaphane-rich broccoli sprouts reduce colonization and attenuate gastritis in Helicobacter pylori-infected mice and humans
references.finding: 70 g/day broccoli sprouts for 8 weeks lowered H. pylori and gastritis markers; values returned to baseline 2 months after stopping.

references.authors: Traka MH, Melchini A, Coode-Bate J, et al.
references.title: Transcriptional changes in prostate of men on active surveillance after a 12-mo glucoraphanin-rich broccoli intervention-results from the Effect of Sulforaphane on prostate CAncer PrEvention (ESCAPE) randomized controlled trial
references.finding: A weekly portion of high-glucoraphanin broccoli soup for 12 months dose-dependently attenuated cancer-linked gene-expression changes in prostate tissue.

references.authors: Armah CN, Derdemezis C, Traka MH, et al.
references.title: Diet rich in high glucoraphanin broccoli reduces plasma LDL cholesterol: Evidence from randomised controlled trials
references.finding: 400 g/week of high-glucoraphanin broccoli for 12 weeks lowered LDL cholesterol 5-7%.

references.authors: Fahey JW, Holtzclaw WD, Wehage SL, et al.
references.title: Sulforaphane Bioavailability from Glucoraphanin-Rich Broccoli: Control by Active Endogenous Myrosinase
references.finding: Sprouts or seeds with active myrosinase gave 3-4-fold more sulforaphane than glucoraphanin without the enzyme.

references.authors: Okunade O, Niranjan K, Ghawi SK, et al.
references.title: Supplementation of the Diet by Exogenous Myrosinase via Mustard Seeds to Increase the Bioavailability of Sulforaphane in Healthy Human Subjects after the Consumption of Cooked Broccoli
references.finding: Adding 1 g brown mustard powder to 200 g cooked broccoli raised 24 h urinary sulforaphane metabolites about 4.5-fold.

references.authors: Navarro SL, Schwarz Y, Song X, et al.
references.title: Cruciferous vegetables have variable effects on biomarkers of systemic inflammation in a randomized controlled trial in healthy young adults
references.finding: Fourteen days of a double-dose crucifer diet lowered serum IL-6 19%; CRP and TNF did not change.

references.authors: Hecht SS, Chung FL, Richie JP Jr, et al.
references.title: Effects of watercress consumption on metabolism of a tobacco-specific lung carcinogen in smokers
references.finding: Watercress at each meal for 3 days raised detoxified NNK metabolites by 33.5% on days 2-3; levels returned to near baseline 1-2 weeks later.

references.authors: Gill CI, Haldar S, Boyd LA, et al.
references.title: Watercress supplementation in diet reduces lymphocyte DNA damage and alters blood antioxidant status in healthy adults
references.finding: 85 g/day raw watercress for 8 weeks cut lymphocyte DNA damage 17% and oxidative purine damage 24%.

references.authors: Michnovicz JJ, Adlercreutz H, Bradlow HL
references.title: Changes in levels of urinary estrogen metabolites after oral indole-3-carbinol treatment in humans
references.finding: Oral I3C (6-7 mg/kg/day) shifted urinary estrogen metabolites toward 2-hydroxylation after 1 week in men and 2 months in women.

references.authors: Bell MC, Crowley-Nowick P, Bradlow HL, et al.
references.title: Placebo-controlled trial of indole-3-carbinol in the treatment of CIN
references.finding: I3C 200-400 mg/day for 12 weeks regressed CIN in 8 of 17 vs 0 of 10 on placebo.

references.authors: Leone A, Bertoli S, Di Lello S, et al.
references.title: Effect of Moringa oleifera Leaf Powder on Postprandial Blood Glucose Response: In Vivo Study on Saharawi People Living in Refugee Camps
references.finding: Adding 20 g moringa leaf powder to a meal lowered post-meal glucose increments at 90-150 min in diabetics only.

references.authors: Nouchi R, Kawata NYS, Saito T, et al.
references.title: Benefits of Wasabi Supplements with 6-MSITC (6-Methylsulfinyl Hexyl Isothiocyanate) on Memory Functioning in Healthy Adults Aged 60 Years and Older: Evidence from a Double-Blinded Randomized Controlled Trial
references.finding: A wasabi 6-MSITC supplement for 12 weeks improved working and episodic memory.

references.authors: Manach C, Williamson G, Morand C, et al.
references.title: Bioavailability and bioefficacy of polyphenols in humans. I. Review of 97 bioavailability studies
references.finding: Across 97 studies, polyphenol metabolites reach only 0-4 µmol/L in plasma after 50 mg; most peak within hours and are cleared quickly, with large differences between compounds.

references.authors: Heiss C, Finis D, Kleinbongard P, et al.
references.title: Sustained increase in flow-mediated dilation after daily intake of high-flavanol cocoa drink over 1 week
references.finding: Single doses of high-flavanol cocoa raised FMD with a peak at 2 h; with daily intake, fasting FMD rose stepwise on days 3, 5 and 8 and returned to baseline after a 1-week washout.

references.authors: Balzer J, Rassaf T, Heiss C, et al.
references.title: Sustained benefits in vascular function through flavanol-containing cocoa in medicated diabetic patients a double-masked, randomized, controlled trial
references.finding: Thrice-daily flavanol cocoa for 30 days raised fasting FMD 30% and acute post-dose FMD rises persisted with no tachyphylaxis.

references.authors: Heiss C, Jahn S, Taylor M, et al.
references.title: Improvement of endothelial function with dietary flavanols is associated with mobilization of circulating angiogenic cells in patients with coronary artery disease
references.finding: High-flavanol cocoa twice daily for 30 days improved FMD 47% and lowered systolic BP 4.2 mmHg vs low-flavanol.

references.authors: Schroeter H, Heiss C, Balzer J, et al.
references.title: (-)-Epicatechin mediates beneficial effects of flavanol-rich cocoa on vascular function in humans
references.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
references.finding: Cocoa flavanols, specifically epicatechin, acutely raised NO species and FMD within hours of ingestion.

references.authors: Sesso HD, Manson JE, Aragaki AK, et al.
references.title: Effect of cocoa flavanol supplementation for the prevention of cardiovascular disease events: the COcoa Supplement and Multivitamin Outcomes Study (COSMOS) randomized clinical trial
references.finding: Cocoa extract (500 mg flavanols/day) for a median 3.6 years did not significantly cut total CVD events (HR 0.90, 0.78-1.02); CVD death HR 0.73; per-protocol HR 0.85.

references.authors: Ottaviani JI, Schroeter H, Bier DM, et al.
references.title: The overlooked impact of background diet and adherence in nutrition trials
references.finding: In COSMOS, about a third of the cocoa group did not reach expected flavanol biomarker levels and 20% of the placebo group had high background intake; biomarker-based analyses gave larger effects (major CVD HR 0.48).

references.authors: McDermott MM, Criqui MH, Domanchuk K, et al.
references.title: Cocoa to Improve Walking Performance in Older People With Peripheral Artery Disease: The COCOA-PAD Pilot Randomized Clinical Trial
references.finding: Daily cocoa for 6 months improved 6-minute walk by 42.6 m when tested 2.5 h after a dose but only 18 m (not significant) at 24 h.

references.authors: Sun Y, Zimmermann D, De Castro CA, et al.
references.title: Dose-response relationship between cocoa flavanols and human endothelial function: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials
references.finding: Cocoa flavanols improved FMD by 1.17%, with an inverted-U dose response peaking near 710 mg/day; most trials had high risk of bias.

references.authors: Rodriguez-Mateos A, Rendeiro C, Bergillos-Meca T, et al.
references.title: Intake and time dependence of blueberry flavonoid-induced improvements in vascular function: a randomized, controlled, double-blind, crossover intervention study with mechanistic insights into biological activity
references.finding: Blueberry polyphenols raised FMD biphasically at 1-2 h and 6 h after intake, tracking plasma metabolites; effects plateaued above ~766 mg polyphenols.

references.authors: Curtis PJ, van der Velpen V, Berends L, et al.
references.title: Blueberries improve biomarkers of cardiometabolic function in participants with metabolic syndrome-results from a 6-month, double-blind, randomized controlled trial
references.finding: One cup (150 g) of blueberries daily for 6 months gave sustained improvements in FMD, arterial stiffness and HDL; half a cup did nothing.

references.authors: Czank C, Cassidy A, Zhang Q, et al.
references.title: Human metabolism and elimination of the anthocyanin, cyanidin-3-glucoside: a (13)C-tracer study
references.finding: 13C-labelled cyanidin-3-glucoside metabolites stayed in the circulation up to 48 h, with half-lives of 12-52 h; relative bioavailability ~12%.

references.authors: Lee MJ, Maliakal P, Chen L, et al.
references.title: Pharmacokinetics of tea catechins after ingestion of green tea and (-)-epigallocatechin-3-gallate by humans: formation of different metabolites and individual variability
references.finding: After green tea, EGCG, EGC and EC peaked at 1.3-1.6 h with half-lives of 3.4, 1.7 and 2.0 h; over 90% of urinary EGC/EC was excreted within 8 h.

references.authors: Chow HH, Cai Y, Hakim IA, et al.
references.title: Pharmacokinetics and safety of green tea polyphenols after multiple-dose administration of epigallocatechin gallate and polyphenon E in healthy individuals
references.finding: Four weeks of 800 mg EGCG once daily raised the EGCG area under the curve by over 60%; 400 mg twice daily did not change kinetics.

references.authors: EFSA Panel on Food Additives and Nutrient Sources added to Food (ANS), Younes M, Aggett P, et al.
references.title: Scientific opinion on the safety of green tea catechins
references.finding: EFSA concluded that 800 mg EGCG/day or more from supplements raises serum transaminases in trials; brewed tea is generally safe, with rare idiosyncratic liver injury.

references.authors: Yu Z, Samavat H, Dostal AM, et al.
references.title: Effect of Green Tea Supplements on Liver Enzyme Elevation: Results from a Randomized Intervention Study in the United States
references.finding: Green tea extract (~843 mg EGCG/day) for 12 months raised ALT; liver function abnormalities had a median onset of 106 days (56-365), ALT normalized a mean 32 days after stopping and rose again on rechallenge.

references.authors: Hakim IA, Harris RB, Brown S, et al.
references.title: Effect of increased tea consumption on oxidative DNA damage among smokers: a randomized controlled study
references.finding: Four cups/day of decaffeinated green tea for 4 months cut urinary 8-OHdG 31%; black tea had no effect.

references.authors: Grassi D, Mulder TP, Draijer R, et al.
references.title: Black tea consumption dose-dependently improves flow-mediated dilation in healthy males
references.finding: One-week periods of black tea (100-800 mg flavonoids/day) dose-dependently raised FMD from 7.8% to 10.3%.

references.authors: Hodgson JM, Woodman RJ, Puddey IB, et al.
references.title: Short-term effects of polyphenol-rich black tea on blood pressure in men and women
references.finding: One day of polyphenol-rich black tea did not change 24 h blood pressure, whereas the same group had earlier found lower BP after 6 months of regular intake.

references.authors: Stalmach A, Mullen W, Barron D, et al.
references.title: Metabolite profiling of hydroxycinnamate derivatives in plasma and urine after the ingestion of coffee by humans: identification of biomarkers of coffee consumption
references.finding: After coffee, some chlorogenic acid metabolites peaked within 1 h (small intestine) and others after 4 h (colonic); 29% of intake was excreted in 24 h.

references.authors: Bakuradze T, Lang R, Hofmann T, et al.
references.title: Coffee consumption rapidly reduces background DNA strand breaks in healthy humans: Results of a short-term repeated uptake intervention study
references.finding: Coffee (200 mL every 2 h) reduced background DNA strand breaks within 2 h of the first cup, falling by about one third over 8 h.

references.authors: Bakuradze T, Lang R, Hofmann T, et al.
references.title: Consumption of a dark roast coffee decreases the level of spontaneous DNA strand breaks: a randomized controlled trial
references.finding: 750 mL/day dark-roast coffee for 4 weeks lowered spontaneous DNA strand breaks by 27% vs water.

references.authors: Shi J, Benowitz NL, Denaro CP, et al.
references.title: Pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic modeling of caffeine: tolerance to pressor effects
references.finding: Tolerance to the blood-pressure-raising effect of caffeine develops and regresses with a half-life of about 1 h and can blunt the effect by over 90%; habitual drinkers regain the response after brief abstinence.

references.authors: Miro-Casas E, Covas MI, Farre M, et al.
references.title: Hydroxytyrosol disposition in humans
references.finding: After 25 mL virgin olive oil, plasma hydroxytyrosol peaked at 32 min (3-O-methyl form at 53 min) with a half-life of 2.43 h; ~98% circulated as conjugates.

references.authors: Covas MI, Nyyssönen K, Poulsen HE, et al.
references.title: The effect of polyphenols in olive oil on heart disease risk factors: a randomized trial
references.finding: In 3-week periods with 2-week washouts, 25 mL/day olive oil raised HDL and lowered oxidized LDL in proportion to phenolic content.

references.authors: Fitó M, Guxens M, Corella D, et al.
references.title: Effect of a traditional Mediterranean diet on lipoprotein oxidation: a randomized controlled trial
references.finding: After 3 months of a Mediterranean diet with virgin olive oil or nuts, oxidized LDL fell (-10.6 and -7.3 U/L) vs no change on a low-fat diet.

references.authors: Estruch R, Ros E, Salas-Salvadó J, et al.
references.title: Primary Prevention of Cardiovascular Disease with a Mediterranean Diet Supplemented with Extra-Virgin Olive Oil or Nuts
references.finding: Republished PREDIMED: over a median 4.8 years, Mediterranean diet with EVOO (HR 0.69) or nuts (HR 0.72) cut major cardiovascular events vs a low-fat control.

references.authors: Agarwal A, Ioannidis JPA
references.title: PREDIMED trial of Mediterranean diet: retracted, republished, still trusted?
references.finding: Critical analysis of the retraction and republication of PREDIMED after randomization irregularities, questioning how much its revised estimates can be trusted.

references.authors: Vareed SK, Kakarala M, Ruffin MT, et al.
references.title: Pharmacokinetics of curcumin conjugate metabolites in healthy human subjects
references.finding: After 10-12 g curcumin, free curcumin was nearly undetectable; conjugates peaked at 3.3 h with a half-life of 6.8 h.

references.authors: Cheng D, Li W, Wang L, et al.
references.title: Pharmacokinetics, Pharmacodynamics, and PKPD Modeling of Curcumin in Regulating Antioxidant and Epigenetic Gene Expression in Healthy Human Volunteers
references.finding: After a single 4 g curcumin dose, leukocyte NRF2, HO-1 and NQO1 mRNA peaked at about 4-6 h; curcumin glucuronide peaked near 2.7 h.

references.authors: Kocher A, Bohnert L, Schiborr C, et al.
references.title: Highly bioavailable micellar curcuminoids accumulate in blood, are safe and do not reduce blood lipids and inflammation markers in moderately hyperlipidemic individuals
references.finding: Micellar curcuminoids (98 mg with each main meal) reached fasting plasma levels of 49 nmol/L within 3 weeks but did not change lipids or inflammation over 6 weeks.

references.authors: Halegoua-DeMarzio D, Navarro V, Ahmad J, et al.
references.title: Liver Injury Associated with Turmeric-A Growing Problem: Ten Cases from the Drug-Induced Liver Injury Network [DILIN]
references.finding: Turmeric-associated liver injury in the US DILIN network was hepatocellular, linked to HLA-B*35:01, with a latency of 1 to 4 months.

references.authors: Alizadeh F, Javadi M, Karami AA, et al.
references.title: Curcumin nanomicelle improves semen parameters, oxidative stress, inflammatory biomarkers, and reproductive hormones in infertile men: A randomized clinical trial
references.finding: 80 mg/day nanomicelle curcumin for 10 weeks improved sperm count, concentration and motility and lowered MDA, CRP and TNF-alpha.

references.authors: Abdelazeem B, Abbas KS, Shehata J, et al.
references.title: The effects of curcumin as dietary supplement for patients with polycystic ovary syndrome: An updated systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials
references.finding: Curcumin improved fasting glucose (-3.7 mg/dL), insulin and HOMA-IR in PCOS, without effects on sex hormones or weight.

references.authors: Walle T, Hsieh F, DeLegge MH, et al.
references.title: High absorption but very low bioavailability of oral resveratrol in humans
references.finding: Oral resveratrol was at least 70% absorbed, but only trace unchanged resveratrol reached plasma; total metabolites had a plasma half-life of 9.2 h.

references.authors: Gliemann L, Schmidt JF, Olesen J, et al.
references.title: Resveratrol blunts the positive effects of exercise training on cardiovascular health in aged men
references.finding: 250 mg/day resveratrol during 8 weeks of training blunted the gain in VO2max by 45% and abolished training effects on blood pressure and lipids.

references.authors: Ochiai A, Kuroda K, Ikemoto Y, et al.
references.title: Influence of resveratrol supplementation on IVF-embryo transfer cycle outcomes
references.finding: Continuous 200 mg/day resveratrol during embryo transfer cycles was associated with lower clinical pregnancy (OR 0.54) and more miscarriage (OR 2.60).

references.authors: Setchell KD, Brown NM, Desai P, et al.
references.title: Bioavailability of pure isoflavones in healthy humans and analysis of commercial soy isoflavone supplements
references.finding: Genistein and daidzein aglycones peaked at 5-7 h and their glycosides at about 9 h after a single dose.

references.authors: Frankenfeld CL, Atkinson C, Thomas WK, et al.
references.title: High concordance of daidzein-metabolizing phenotypes in individuals measured 1 to 3 years apart
references.finding: Equol-producer status was concordant in 82% of people measured 1-3 years apart.

references.authors: Vanegas JC, Afeiche MC, Gaskins AJ, et al.
references.title: Soy food intake and treatment outcomes of women undergoing assisted reproductive technology
references.finding: Higher habitual soy isoflavone intake was associated with higher live birth in ART (OR ~1.8 at 2.6-28 mg/day).

references.authors: Kuijsten A, Arts IC, Vree TB, et al.
references.title: Pharmacokinetics of enterolignans in healthy men and women consuming a single dose of secoisolariciresinol diglucoside
references.finding: After flax lignan (SDG), enterolactone peaked at about 20 h with a half-life of 12.6 h and mean residence time of 36 h; enterolignans accumulate with intake 2-3 times a day.

references.authors: Rodriguez-Leyva D, Weighell W, Edel AL, et al.
references.title: Potent antihypertensive action of dietary flaxseed in hypertensive patients
references.finding: 30 g/day milled flaxseed for 6 months lowered systolic BP ~10 mmHg and diastolic ~7 mmHg vs placebo (15 mmHg systolic in hypertensives).

references.authors: Seeram NP, Zhang Y, McKeever R, et al.
references.title: Pomegranate juice and extracts provide similar levels of plasma and urinary ellagitannin metabolites in human subjects
references.finding: Pomegranate juice ellagic acid peaked in plasma at about 0.65 h; extracts gave similar exposure with a later peak; urolithin A glucuronide appeared in urine.

references.authors: Tomás-Barberán FA, García-Villalba R, González-Sarrías A, et al.
references.title: Ellagic acid metabolism by human gut microbiota: consistent observation of three urolithin phenotypes in intervention trials, independent of food source, age, and health status
references.finding: People fall into three stable urolithin metabotypes (A, B, and non-producers) depending on gut microbiota, independent of food source.

references.authors: Davidson MH, Maki KC, Dicklin MR, et al.
references.title: Effects of consumption of pomegranate juice on carotid intima-media thickness in men and women at moderate risk for coronary heart disease
references.finding: 240 mL/day pomegranate juice for up to 18 months did not slow overall carotid intima-media thickness progression.

references.authors: Manach C, Morand C, Gil-Izquierdo A, et al.
references.title: Bioavailability in humans of the flavanones hesperidin and narirutin after the ingestion of two doses of orange juice

timing.summary: Each serving gives a short sulforaphane pulse (plasma half-life about 2 h), but the enzymes it switches on are long-lived proteins, so the protective effect lasts roughly 1-3 days and then fades. Detox effects appear on day 1 of daily dosing and hold for 12 weeks without tolerance, and they are gone within about 5 days of stopping.

onset.text: Plasma sulforaphane peaks about 1 h after a dose [tfood-ye2002]; benzene detoxication was already up 61% on day 1 [tfood-egner2014], and nasal NQO1/HO-1/GST mRNA rose 2-3-fold after 3 daily doses [tfood-riedl2009].

full.text: Detox biomarkers reach their full effect within the first day and stay flat for 12 weeks [tfood-egner2014]; induced skin NQO1 keeps stacking over the first few daily doses (1.5-fold after one, 4.5-fold after three) [tfood-dinkovakostova2007]. Clinical endpoints in trials were read at 8-18 weeks [tfood-yanaka2009, tfood-singh2014].

after_stopping.text: The drug itself is mostly excreted within 8-24 h [tfood-ye2002]. Protection in human skin was 32% at 48 h and 10% at 72 h after the last dose [tfood-talalay2007], and pollutant-detox biomarkers were back to baseline after a 5-day washout [tfood-kensler2012]. Clinical gains reversed over 4-8 weeks off treatment [tfood-singh2014, tfood-yanaka2009].

frequency.text: Every positive human trial dosed daily, and daily dosing showed no tolerance over 12 weeks [tfood-egner2014]. Because induced enzymes persist 1-3 days (NQO1 protein half-life over 18 h [tfood-siegel2001]; protection decays over 2-3 days [tfood-talalay2007, tfood-gao2001]), every other day probably keeps much but not all of the effect; no human trial has compared schedules, and every-other-day dosing worked in mice [tfood-xu2016]. Splitting the same daily amount into two doses raised plasma exposure but not blood-cell markers [tfood-atwell2015].

timing.debate: How long the effect lasts is contested by method: cell and skin studies show enzyme-mediated protection persisting for days [tfood-gao2001, tfood-talalay2007], while the Qidong crossover found no carryover after 5 days [tfood-kensler2012]. Nrf2 induces its own inhibitor KEAP1, which predicts damping with constant stimulation [tfood-lee2007], yet 12 weeks of daily dosing showed no attenuation [tfood-egner2014]. Some argue for blending glucoraphanin and sulforaphane to get both a peak and steady exposure [tfood-egner2011], but split dosing changed no blood-cell marker [tfood-atwell2015].

timing.summary: With active myrosinase, seed powder behaves like sprouts: a sulforaphane pulse within hours that is cleared in about a day, with downstream enzyme effects lasting a few days. Without the enzyme, conversion depends on gut bacteria and is slower, lower and more drawn out.

onset.text: Sulforaphane from seeds or sprouts with active enzyme appears within hours and is 3-4 times more bioavailable than glucoraphanin without enzyme [tfood-fahey2015]; enzyme induction follows within a day (extrapolated from sprout data [tfood-egner2014]).

full.text: No time course with seed powder itself; sprout and beverage trials reached their full detox effect within a day [tfood-egner2014].

after_stopping.text: Sulforaphane is cleared within about a day [tfood-ye2002]; enzyme-mediated protection fades over 2-5 days by analogy with sprout data [tfood-talalay2007, tfood-kensler2012].

frequency.text: Preformed sulforaphane gives a bolus, while glucoraphanin without enzyme gives a slower, steadier exposure [tfood-egner2011]. No trial has compared daily with intermittent seed powder; daily is what was tested in sprout and extract trials.

timing.debate: Whether a steady low exposure (glucoraphanin converted by gut bacteria) or a sharp peak (preformed sulforaphane) is better is unresolved; Egner et al. propose blends [tfood-egner2011], while the greater, more consistent delivery with active enzyme [tfood-fahey2015] favours the bolus form.

timing.summary: Each capsule is a pulse cleared within a day, but blood glutathione and Nrf2-target mRNA rise within days to weeks of daily use. Clinical effects in trials took 4-18 weeks to show and faded within weeks of stopping.

onset.text: Blood-cell HMOX1, NQO1 and glutathione rose within 7 days to 1 month of daily dosing [tfood-sedlak2018, tfood-doss2016, tfood-ribeiro2024]; nasal inflammation to diesel particles fell after 4 days [tfood-heber2014].

full.text: Behavioural effects in autism were measured at 18 weeks [tfood-singh2014]; no trial mapped when biomarkers plateau beyond the first days of dosing.

after_stopping.text: Autism behaviour scores rose back toward baseline during 4 weeks off sulforaphane [tfood-singh2014]; detox biomarkers lose the effect within 5 days [tfood-kensler2012].

frequency.text: Trials dosed daily; one or two doses a day gave the same blood-cell marker response [tfood-atwell2015]. Every-other-day dosing is untested in humans (it worked in mice [tfood-xu2016]).

sperm.late_start: Unknown: no human data. Because Nrf2 induction appears within a day, a late start could in theory protect sperm already maturing, but this is untested.
sperm.text: No human sperm trial exists. Sperm take about 64 days (range 42-76) from labelled precursor to ejaculate [tfood-misell2006], and the classic ~74-day estimate is uncertain by about a week [tfood-amann2008], so a diet change needs roughly 2.5-3 months to reach every stage of the sperm in a given ejaculate.

egg.late_start: Unknown: no human data on eggs or IVF.
egg.text: No human egg or IVF trial exists. A follicle grows for several months before ovulation, including about 70 days from the preantral stage to 2 mm [tfood-gougeon2010], so anything acting on the growing follicle needs roughly 3-4 months to cover the whole final growth phase.

timing.debate: Lasting benefit is questioned: autism gains reverted within weeks of stopping [tfood-singh2014], and Nrf2 feedback could limit long-term activation [tfood-lee2007], although 12 weeks of daily dosing showed no tolerance [tfood-egner2014]. Permanent maximal Nrf2 activation is harmful in mice [tfood-wakabayashi2003], an argument against chasing constant high exposure.

timing.summary: A raw broccoli meal gives a sulforaphane peak at about 1.6 h (cooked: about 6 h) that is cleared within a day. Yet trials using broccoli only a few times a week (400 g per week, or one soup portion weekly) still lowered LDL over 12 weeks and changed prostate gene expression over a year.

onset.text: Plasma sulforaphane peaks 1.6 h after raw and 6 h after cooked broccoli, with excretion half-lives of 2.4-2.6 h [tfood-vermeulen2008].

full.text: LDL fell 5-7% after 12 weeks of 400 g/week high-glucoraphanin broccoli [tfood-armah2015]; prostate gene-expression changes were attenuated over 12 months of weekly soup [tfood-traka2019]. Earlier time points were not measured.

after_stopping.text: Not measured for LDL or gene expression; the sulforaphane itself is cleared within a day [tfood-vermeulen2008].

frequency.text: The two outcome trials used broccoli a few times a week (400 g/week) or weekly [tfood-armah2015, tfood-traka2019], so daily intake is not required for these effects; no trial compared schedules.

timing.debate: No substantive published debate on timing found.

timing.summary: Isothiocyanates from kale, cabbage and Brussels sprouts are short-lived like sulforaphane, but a 14-day controlled crucifer diet lowered IL-6. What happens after stopping was not measured.

onset.text: Serum IL-6 was 19% lower after 14 days of a double-dose crucifer diet; earlier time points were not measured [tfood-navarro2014].

full.text: Not measured beyond 14 days in feeding trials.

after_stopping.text: Not measured; isothiocyanates are cleared within a day [tfood-ye2002].

frequency.text: The feeding trial gave crucifers daily [tfood-navarro2014]; schedule comparisons do not exist.

timing.debate: No substantive published debate on timing found.

timing.summary: Mustard powder works within the same meal: it restores the enzyme that cooking destroys and raised sulforaphane output from cooked broccoli about 4.5-fold over the next 24 h. It has no effect of its own beyond that meal.

onset.text: Same meal: sulforaphane metabolites in 24 h urine rose about 4.5-fold [tfood-okunade2018].

full.text: Complete within the 24 h after the meal [tfood-okunade2018].

after_stopping.text: No carryover beyond the meal it is added to.

frequency.text: Add it to each cooked crucifer meal; it only affects that meal [tfood-okunade2018].

timing.debate: No substantive published debate on timing found.

timing.summary: Watercress shifted a tobacco carcinogen toward detoxification within 2-3 days, and the effect was gone 1-2 weeks after stopping. A drop in DNA damage was seen after 8 weeks of daily intake.

onset.text: Detoxified NNK metabolites rose 33.5% on days 2-3 of eating watercress at each meal [tfood-hecht1995].

full.text: Lymphocyte DNA damage was 17% lower after 8 weeks of 85 g/day (the only time point) [tfood-gill2007].

after_stopping.text: NNK detox metabolites were back near baseline 1-2 weeks after stopping [tfood-hecht1995].

frequency.text: Both trials used daily or every-meal intake [tfood-hecht1995, tfood-gill2007]; the detox effect fades within a week or two, so regular intake is needed to keep it.

timing.debate: No substantive published debate on timing found.

timing.summary: The only human outcome trial gave a wasabi isothiocyanate supplement daily for 12 weeks and measured memory only at the end. When effects start and how long they last are unknown.

onset.text: Not measured; memory improved at the single 12-week assessment [tfood-nouchi2023].

full.text: Not measured beyond 12 weeks [tfood-nouchi2023].

after_stopping.text: Not measured.

frequency.text: The trial used a daily supplement [tfood-nouchi2023]; no schedule data.

timing.debate: No substantive published debate on timing found.

timing.summary: Moringa leaf powder blunted the blood-glucose rise of the meal it was eaten with, in people with diabetes. Longer-term effects are unproven, so there is no known build-up or persistence.

onset.text: Lower post-meal glucose increments at 90-150 min with 20 g leaf powder in the meal [tfood-leone2018].

full.text: Not measured beyond the single meal.

after_stopping.text: Not measured; the measured effect is confined to that meal.

frequency.text: Acts per meal [tfood-leone2018]; chronic benefit unproven.

timing.debate: No substantive published debate on timing found.

timing.summary: I3C shifts estrogen metabolism toward 2-hydroxylation within a week, through enzyme induction. The one lesion-regression trial ran 12 weeks; persistence after stopping was not measured.

onset.text: Urinary estrogen metabolites shifted after 1 week in men (and at 2 months in women) [tfood-michnovicz1997].

full.text: CIN regression was assessed at 12 weeks [tfood-bell2000].

after_stopping.text: Not measured.

frequency.text: Trials dosed daily [tfood-michnovicz1997, tfood-bell2000].

timing.debate: No substantive published debate on timing found.

timing.summary: Tea catechins peak 1-2 h after a cup and are mostly gone within 8 h, so each cup is a short pulse. Lower oxidative DNA damage in smokers was seen after 4 months of 4 cups a day.

onset.text: Catechins peak at 1.3-1.6 h with half-lives of 1.7-3.4 h; over 90% of urinary EGC/EC is excreted within 8 h [tfood-lee2002].

full.text: Urinary 8-OHdG was 31% lower after 4 months of 4 cups/day in heavy smokers [tfood-hakim2003].

after_stopping.text: Catechins clear within a day [tfood-lee2002]; persistence of the DNA-damage effect was not measured.

frequency.text: Because catechins clear within hours [tfood-lee2002], benefits seen in trials came from several cups every day [tfood-hakim2003].

timing.debate: No substantive published debate on timing found.

timing.summary: High-dose extract (about 800 mg EGCG a day) raises liver enzymes after a median of about 3.5 months, and the liver recovers about a month after stopping. Once-daily bolus dosing makes exposure climb over the first weeks.

onset.text: Liver-function abnormalities appeared a median 106 days (range 56-365) after starting ~843 mg EGCG/day [tfood-yu2017]; EFSA links ≥800 mg/day to transaminase rises [tfood-efsa2018].

full.text: EGCG exposure (AUC) rose over 60% after 4 weeks of once-daily 800 mg, but not with 400 mg twice daily [tfood-chow2003].

after_stopping.text: ALT returned to normal a mean 32 days (13-92) after stopping, and rose again in most women who restarted [tfood-yu2017].

frequency.text: Avoid high-dose extracts; if used, a split dose avoids the exposure build-up seen with a single daily bolus [tfood-chow2003].

timing.debate: EFSA sets the transaminase threshold at 800 mg EGCG/day from supplements [tfood-efsa2018], but idiosyncratic injury has a different, unpredictable timing that a dose threshold does not capture.

timing.summary: Black tea improved flow-mediated dilation within a week of daily drinking, but a single day of tea did not lower 24 h blood pressure. The blood-pressure benefit that the same group saw needed months of regular intake.

onset.text: FMD was higher after 1-week periods of twice-daily black tea, even at 100 mg flavonoids/day [tfood-grassi2009].

full.text: One day of tea did not change 24 h BP, whereas 6 months of regular intake did [tfood-hodgson2013].

after_stopping.text: Not measured.

frequency.text: Benefits came from daily drinking [tfood-grassi2009, tfood-hodgson2013].

timing.debate: No substantive published debate on timing found.

timing.summary: Coffee lowered background DNA strand breaks within 2 h of the first cup, and four weeks of 3-4 cups a day held a 27% reduction. Chlorogenic acid metabolites arrive in two waves (about 1 h and after 4 h) and clear within a day, so the effect depends on regular intake.

onset.text: DNA strand breaks fell within 2 h of the first cup [tfood-bakuradze2016]; chlorogenic acid metabolites peak within 1 h and again after 4 h [tfood-stalmach2009].

full.text: A cumulative reduction of about a third over 8 h of repeated cups [tfood-bakuradze2016]; 27% lower than water after 4 weeks [tfood-bakuradze2015].

after_stopping.text: Not measured for DNA damage. Caffeine's blood-pressure tolerance regresses within hours of abstinence [tfood-shi1993].

frequency.text: Benefit was shown with cups spread through the day, every day [tfood-bakuradze2016, tfood-bakuradze2015]. Tolerance to caffeine's pressor effect builds and fades within hours, so regular drinkers see little blood-pressure rise while occasional drinkers see more [tfood-shi1993].

timing.debate: No substantive published debate on timing found.

timing.summary: Each flavanol dose improves artery function within 2 h, and daily intake also raises the fasting baseline within 3-8 days, without tolerance over 30 days. The gain is gone a week after stopping, and in a 6-month trial walking improved much more 2.5 h after a dose than 24 h after.

onset.text: FMD peaks about 2 h after a dose [tfood-heiss2007, tfood-schroeter2006].

full.text: Fasting FMD rose on days 3, 5 and 8 of daily intake [tfood-heiss2007]; 30 days of thrice-daily cocoa kept both the raised baseline and the post-dose rises, with no tachyphylaxis [tfood-balzer2008].

after_stopping.text: Fasting FMD was back to baseline after a 1-week cocoa-free washout [tfood-heiss2007]; in PAD, the walking gain was 42.6 m at 2.5 h but only 18 m at 24 h after the last dose [tfood-mcdermott2020].

frequency.text: The effect is largely dose-timed: trials used one to three doses a day [tfood-heiss2010, tfood-balzer2008], and benefit faded by 24 h [tfood-mcdermott2020]. In COSMOS a third of the cocoa group did not reach expected biomarker levels, and adherence-based analyses showed larger effects [tfood-ottaviani2025].

timing.debate: Short trials show reliable vascular effects [tfood-sun2019], but the 3.6-year COSMOS trial missed its primary endpoint (HR 0.90) [tfood-sesso2022]; a biomarker re-analysis by investigators including industry-affiliated authors argues poor adherence and background flavanol intake hid a larger effect [tfood-ottaviani2025].

timing.summary: Blueberries improve artery function in two waves, at 1-2 h and 6 h, as phenolic metabolites circulate; some metabolites stay in blood up to 48 h. A cup a day for 6 months kept a sustained improvement, while half a cup did nothing.

onset.text: FMD rose at 1-2 h and again at 6 h after blueberry polyphenols [tfood-rodriguezmateos2013].

full.text: Sustained FMD and arterial-stiffness improvements after 6 months of 150 g/day [tfood-curtis2019]; intermediate time points not reported.

after_stopping.text: Anthocyanin metabolites persist up to 48 h, with half-lives of 12-52 h [tfood-czank2013]; vascular persistence after stopping was not measured.

frequency.text: The positive 6-month trial used a cup every day [tfood-curtis2019]; metabolites clear within about 2 days [tfood-czank2013].

timing.debate: No substantive published debate on timing found.

timing.summary: No timing study exists for blackberries themselves. By analogy with other anthocyanin berries, effects should come within hours of eating and fade within about 2 days.

onset.text: Extrapolated from blueberries: vascular effects at 1-2 h and 6 h [tfood-rodriguezmateos2013].

full.text: Not measured for blackberries.

after_stopping.text: Extrapolated: anthocyanin metabolites clear within about 48 h [tfood-czank2013].

frequency.text: Extrapolated from berry trials that used daily intake [tfood-curtis2019].

timing.debate: No substantive published debate on timing found.

timing.summary: Berry anthocyanins act on blood vessels within hours and their metabolites linger in blood for up to 2 days. Lipid and blood-pressure effects in trials took weeks of regular intake.

onset.text: Vascular effects at 1-2 h and 6 h after berry polyphenols [tfood-rodriguezmateos2013].

full.text: Sustained vascular and HDL effects needed daily intake over months in the longest berry trial [tfood-curtis2019].

after_stopping.text: Anthocyanin metabolites persist up to 48 h [tfood-czank2013].

frequency.text: Effects track recent intake; daily or near-daily servings were used in trials [tfood-curtis2019].

timing.debate: No substantive published debate on timing found.

timing.summary: Ellagic acid from pomegranate peaks in blood within about an hour and then gut bacteria turn it into urolithins, which only some people make. An 18-month trial found no effect on carotid thickening, so there is no proven benefit to time.

onset.text: Plasma ellagic acid peaks at about 0.65 h after juice [tfood-seeram2008]; urolithin production depends on a person's stable gut metabotype [tfood-tomasbarberan2014].

full.text: No overall effect on carotid intima-media progression after up to 18 months of 240 mL/day [tfood-davidson2009].

after_stopping.text: Not measured.

frequency.text: No outcome benefit has been shown, so there is no evidence-based schedule [tfood-davidson2009].

timing.debate: The null 18-month trial [tfood-davidson2009] contrasts with exploratory benefit in people with high oxidative stress in the same trial; metabotype differences [tfood-tomasbarberan2014] may explain inconsistent responses.

timing.summary: Hesperidin needs gut bacteria to free it, so blood levels peak late (5-7 h) and are gone by 24 h. Microvascular function improved only at that peak, while diastolic blood pressure was lower after 4 weeks of daily orange juice or hesperidin.

onset.text: Flavanone metabolites appear at 3 h, peak at 5-7 h [tfood-manach2003]; microvascular reactivity improved at the hesperetin peak [tfood-morand2011].

full.text: Diastolic BP was lower after 4 weeks of 500 mL/day orange juice or hesperidin [tfood-morand2011].

after_stopping.text: Flavanones return to baseline within 24 h [tfood-manach2003]; BP persistence not measured.

frequency.text: Fasting microvascular function did not improve, only post-dose function did [tfood-morand2011], so the effect depends on regular intake.

timing.debate: No substantive published debate on timing found.

timing.summary: Olive oil phenols peak in blood within an hour and have a half-life of about 2.5 h, but daily use lowered oxidized LDL within 3 weeks. Cardiovascular-event benefit in PREDIMED accrued over about 5 years.

onset.text: Hydroxytyrosol peaks 32-53 min after 25 mL virgin olive oil, half-life 2.43 h [tfood-mirocasas2003].

full.text: Oxidized LDL and HDL changed within 3-week periods in proportion to phenol content [tfood-covas2006]; oxidized LDL fell at 3 months in PREDIMED [tfood-fito2007]; CVD events were lower over a median 4.8 years [tfood-estruch2018].

after_stopping.text: Not directly measured; EUROLIVE assumed reversal within its 2-week washouts [tfood-covas2006].

frequency.text: Phenols clear within hours [tfood-mirocasas2003]; trials used 25 mL every day [tfood-covas2006].

timing.debate: PREDIMED's long-term benefit is debated after its 2013 report was retracted and republished because of randomization problems [tfood-agarwal2019, tfood-estruch2018].

timing.summary: Flax lignans are turned into enterolactone by gut bacteria; it peaks about 20 h after eating and has a half-life of about 13 h, so it accumulates with daily intake. Blood pressure was about 10 mmHg lower after 6 months of 30 g a day.

onset.text: Enterolignans appear in plasma 8-10 h after intake and enterolactone peaks at about 20 h [tfood-kuijsten2005].

full.text: Systolic BP was about 10 mmHg lower after 6 months of 30 g/day milled flax (earlier time points not reported in the abstract) [tfood-rodriguezleyva2013].

after_stopping.text: Enterolactone mean residence time is about 36 h and most is excreted within 3 days [tfood-kuijsten2005]; BP persistence not measured.

frequency.text: Enterolignans reach steady state with intake 2-3 times a day [tfood-kuijsten2005]; the BP trial used daily flax [tfood-rodriguezleyva2013].

timing.debate: No substantive published debate on timing found.

timing.summary: Soy isoflavones peak in blood 5-9 h after eating and clear within about a day. Whether a person makes equol is a stable trait over years, and the fertility association concerns habitual intake rather than timed use.

onset.text: Genistein and daidzein peak 5-9 h after a dose [tfood-setchell2001].

full.text: Not applicable; no timed outcome trial in this group.

after_stopping.text: Isoflavones clear within about a day (extrapolated from their kinetics [tfood-setchell2001]); equol-producer status was concordant in 82% of people 1-3 years apart [tfood-frankenfeld2005].

frequency.text: Associations are with habitual intake [tfood-vanegas2015].

egg.late_start: Unknown; the association is with habitual diet, not a timed start.
egg.text: Higher habitual soy isoflavone intake was linked to higher ART live birth [tfood-vanegas2015]; if causal, it would act over follicle growth (extrapolated). A follicle grows for several months before ovulation, including about 70 days from the preantral stage to 2 mm [tfood-gougeon2010], so anything acting on the growing follicle needs roughly 3-4 months to cover the whole final growth phase.

timing.debate: No substantive published debate on timing found.

timing.summary: Resveratrol is well absorbed but almost all is conjugated at once; only metabolites circulate, with a half-life of about 9 h. A glass of wine supplies far too little for any timed effect.

onset.text: Metabolites peak within hours of a 25 mg dose; unchanged resveratrol is only a trace [tfood-walle2004].

full.text: Not applicable.

after_stopping.text: Metabolites have a plasma half-life of 9.2 h, so they clear within about 2 days [tfood-walle2004].

frequency.text: No antioxidant reason to drink on any schedule [tfood-walle2004].

timing.debate: No substantive published debate on timing found.

timing.summary: Resveratrol metabolites clear within about 2 days, but daily use during 8 weeks of training blunted fitness and blood-pressure gains. Continuous use during embryo-transfer cycles was linked to lower pregnancy rates.

onset.text: Training blunting was measured after 8 weeks of 250 mg/day [tfood-gliemann2013].

full.text: Not measured beyond 8 weeks [tfood-gliemann2013].

after_stopping.text: Metabolite half-life 9.2 h [tfood-walle2004], so drug exposure ends within about 2 days; recovery of training response not measured.

frequency.text: Avoid during training blocks [tfood-gliemann2013] and during IVF embryo transfer [tfood-ochiai2019].

egg.late_start: Stopping before the embryo-transfer cycle starts is what matters; the drug clears within about 2 days [tfood-walle2004].
egg.text: Harm was linked to use during embryo transfer cycles (OR 0.54 for pregnancy) [tfood-ochiai2019], i.e. at the endometrium and implantation, so stop before that cycle (extrapolated).

timing.debate: No head-to-head timing debate found; the training-blunting result rests on one 27-man, 8-week trial [tfood-gliemann2013] and the IVF harm on a retrospective study only [tfood-ochiai2019], so neither the onset nor the safe stopping interval is well defined.

timing.summary: Culinary or capsule curcumin barely reaches blood as free curcumin; its conjugates peak at about 3 h with a half-life of about 7 h. Leukocyte Nrf2-target mRNA peaked 4-6 h after a large single dose, so any effect is short-lived.

onset.text: Conjugates peak at about 3 h [tfood-vareed2008]; leukocyte NRF2, HO-1 and NQO1 mRNA peaked 4-6 h after 4 g curcumin [tfood-cheng2019].

full.text: No long-term human outcome data for culinary turmeric.

after_stopping.text: Conjugate half-life about 6.8 h [tfood-vareed2008], so exposure ends within about 2 days.

frequency.text: No outcome-based schedule exists for culinary use.

timing.debate: No substantive published debate on timing found.

timing.summary: Enhanced-absorption curcumin builds a measurable fasting blood level within 3 weeks of taking it with each meal. Semen changes were seen after 10 weeks; liver injury, when it happens, appears 1-4 months in.

onset.text: Fasting plasma curcuminoids reached 49 nmol/L within 3 weeks of micellar dosing with meals [tfood-kocher2016]; Nrf2-target mRNA in leukocytes peaks 4-6 h after a dose [tfood-cheng2019].

full.text: Semen and inflammation changes at 10 weeks [tfood-alizadeh2018]; lipid and inflammation markers did not change by 6 weeks in hyperlipidemia [tfood-kocher2016].

after_stopping.text: Conjugate half-life about 7 h [tfood-vareed2008]; clinical persistence not measured.

frequency.text: Trials dosed daily, often with each meal [tfood-kocher2016, tfood-alizadeh2018]. Liver injury linked to turmeric products had a latency of 1-4 months [tfood-halegoua2023].

sperm.late_start: Unknown; the trial measured only at 10 weeks.
sperm.text: The single RCT ran 10 weeks, about one spermatogenic cycle [tfood-alizadeh2018]. Sperm take about 64 days (range 42-76) from labelled precursor to ejaculate [tfood-misell2006], and the classic ~74-day estimate is uncertain by about a week [tfood-amann2008], so a diet change needs roughly 2.5-3 months to reach every stage of the sperm in a given ejaculate.

egg.late_start: Unknown; PCOS trials measured metabolic markers, not eggs.
egg.text: PCOS trials improved glucose and insulin [tfood-abdelazeem2022]; no egg or IVF outcome data. A follicle grows for several months before ovulation, including about 70 days from the preantral stage to 2 mm [tfood-gougeon2010], so anything acting on the growing follicle needs roughly 3-4 months to cover the whole final growth phase.

timing.debate: No substantive published debate on timing found.

timing.summary: Most polyphenols peak in blood within a few hours at low micromolar levels and are cleared within a day, so any capsule effect is pulsatile. A few gut-derived metabolites (lignans, anthocyanin breakdown products) last 1-2 days.

onset.text: Plasma metabolites peak within hours at 0-4 µmol/L [tfood-manach2005].

full.text: Not applicable; no outcome benefit established.

after_stopping.text: Most clear within a day; some colonic metabolites persist 1-2 days [tfood-manach2005, tfood-czank2013, tfood-kuijsten2005].

frequency.text: No outcome-based schedule exists [tfood-manach2005].

timing.debate: No substantive published debate on timing found.

timing.summary: Garlic supplements lower blood pressure in trials lasting weeks, and cholesterol effects needed more than 2 months. Persistence after stopping is not known.

onset.text: BP lowering in trials of a few weeks or more [tfood-ried2016].

full.text: Cholesterol lowering required more than 2 months of intake [tfood-ried2016].

after_stopping.text: Not measured.

frequency.text: Trials gave garlic daily [tfood-ried2016].

timing.debate: No substantive published debate on timing found.

timing.summary: Spices act mostly in the pan: they cut oxidation products formed while cooking and lowered the eaters' urinary MDA after that meal. There is no build-up or carryover.

onset.text: Same meal: meat MDA -71% and urinary MDA -49% after a spiced burger [tfood-li2010].

full.text: Complete within the meal [tfood-li2010].

after_stopping.text: No carryover beyond the meal.

frequency.text: Use with each meal that needs it, especially grilled or fried meat [tfood-li2010].

timing.debate: No substantive published debate on timing found.

timing.summary: Nitrate from leafy greens lowers blood pressure within 2.5-3 h, with some effect left at 24 h, and daily intake lowered home blood pressure within a week with no tolerance over 4 weeks. Blood pressure drifts back up within 2 weeks of stopping.

onset.text: Peak BP fall at 2.5-3 h after a nitrate load (about -10/-8 mmHg) [tfood-webb2008].

full.text: Home BP fell within 1 week of daily nitrate and stayed down for 4 weeks without tachyphylaxis [tfood-kapil2015].

after_stopping.text: About 6 mmHg systolic still lower at 24 h after a single dose [tfood-webb2008]; BP started returning toward baseline during a 2-week washout [tfood-kapil2015].

frequency.text: Effects peak hours after intake and fade over a day or so [tfood-webb2008]; daily intake held the reduction [tfood-kapil2015]. Pooled short trials show about -4.4 mmHg systolic [tfood-siervo2013].

timing.debate: No substantive published debate on timing found.

timing.summary: Doubling produce intake lowered oxidative DNA and lipid damage markers within 2 weeks in one trial, but 600 g a day for 24 days did nothing in healthy nonsmokers. Disease benefits in cohorts reflect years of intake.

onset.text: Lymphocyte and urinary 8-OHdG and urinary isoprostanes fell after 14 days at 12 servings/day [tfood-thompson1999].

full.text: Mortality associations reflect long-term intake up to ~800 g/day [tfood-aune2017]; no trial mapped the plateau.

after_stopping.text: Not measured; 24 days of complete produce depletion did not raise oxidative DNA damage either [tfood-moller2003].

frequency.text: Benefits are associated with habitual daily intake [tfood-aune2017].

sperm.text: High-pesticide-residue produce was associated with lower sperm count in semen collected up to 18 months after diet assessment [tfood-chiu2015]. Sperm take about 64 days (range 42-76) from labelled precursor to ejaculate [tfood-misell2006], and the classic ~74-day estimate is uncertain by about a week [tfood-amann2008], so a diet change needs roughly 2.5-3 months to reach every stage of the sperm in a given ejaculate.

timing.debate: Short-term trials disagree: 14 days of doubled produce lowered oxidative markers [tfood-thompson1999], while 24 days of 600 g/day did not [tfood-moller2003].

timing.summary: Dehydration is an acute state: 24 h of fluid restriction raised muscle H2O2 during exercise. Rehydrating should reverse it within hours, though that was not measured.

onset.text: Raised muscle H2O2 and stress signalling after 24 h of fluid restriction [tfood-luk2025].

full.text: Not measured.

after_stopping.text: Not measured; recovery with rehydration is expected within hours to a day (extrapolated).

frequency.text: Drink to thirst every day; dehydration effects are acute [tfood-luk2025].

timing.debate: No substantive published debate on timing found.

timing.summary: There are no human data on eggplant and oxidative stress, so nothing is known about timing. The only evidence is test-tube antioxidant activity of nasunin.

onset.text: Not measured in humans [tfood-noda2000].

full.text: Not measured.

after_stopping.text: Not measured.

frequency.text: No human evidence to base a schedule on.

timing.debate: No substantive published debate on timing found.

timing.summary: Urinary pesticide metabolites fall within days of switching to organic food, because most current pesticides clear quickly. They would rise again within days of switching back; health effects, if any, would take years.

onset.text: Pesticide metabolites fell significantly between day 1 and day 6 of an organic diet [tfood-gonzalez2023], by up to 95% in a family study [tfood-hyland2019].

full.text: Reached within the first week [tfood-gonzalez2023, tfood-hyland2019].

after_stopping.text: Not measured; given the fast fall, levels would be expected to return within days of resuming conventional food (extrapolated).

frequency.text: Exposure tracks recent meals, so the reduction lasts only while the diet lasts [tfood-hyland2019].

timing.debate: No substantive published debate on timing found.

timing.summary: A single oral dose taken before sun exposure reduced sunburn and DNA damage measured the next day. Nothing is known about daily use or how long protection lasts.

onset.text: A single 7.5 mg/kg dose before UV reduced erythema, sunburn cells and DNA dimers at 24 h [tfood-middelkamphup2004].

full.text: Not measured.

after_stopping.text: Not measured.

frequency.text: Taken before planned sun exposure in the key study [tfood-middelkamphup2004].

timing.debate: No substantive published debate on timing found.

timing.summary: The gut microbiome shifts within a day of a diet change and snaps back within about 2 days of returning to the old diet, while a person's basic enterotype stays put. Over generations, fiber deprivation can permanently lose microbes in mice.

onset.text: Community composition changed within 24 h [tfood-wu2011] and within 1 day of the new food reaching the gut [tfood-david2014].

full.text: Fiber-degrading capacity rose over a 17-week high-fiber diet, with person-specific responses [tfood-wastyk2021].

after_stopping.text: The microbiota reverted to its original structure 2 days after a short diet ended [tfood-david2014]; in mice, losses reversed within one generation but became permanent over several [tfood-sonnenburg2016].

frequency.text: Because the community follows the last few days of food [tfood-david2014], fiber needs to be eaten every day to keep fiber-feeding microbes active.

timing.debate: Short feeding studies show fast, reversible change [tfood-david2014, tfood-wu2011], whereas a mouse study shows cumulative, irreversible loss over generations [tfood-sonnenburg2016]; an 8-week whole-grain trial produced no major microbiome change at all [tfood-roager2019].

timing.summary: Eight weeks of whole grains lowered IL-6, CRP and body weight without major microbiome change. Lower heart disease and mortality in cohorts reflect years of habitual intake.

onset.text: IL-6 and CRP lower after 8 weeks (only time point) [tfood-roager2019].

full.text: Cohort benefits reflect long-term intake [tfood-aune2016]; plateau not measured.

after_stopping.text: Not measured; the crossover used a washout of at least 6 weeks [tfood-roager2019].

frequency.text: Associations are with daily servings (90 g/day = 3 servings) [tfood-aune2016].

timing.debate: No substantive published debate on timing found.

timing.summary: A cup of legumes a day as part of a low-GI diet lowered HbA1c by 0.5% and systolic pressure over 3 months. HbA1c itself integrates about 3 months of glucose, so this is roughly the earliest it can fully show.

onset.text: Not measured before the 3-month endpoint [tfood-jenkins2012].

full.text: HbA1c -0.5% at 3 months [tfood-jenkins2012]; HbA1c reflects about 3 months of glucose exposure (extrapolated from red-cell lifespan).

after_stopping.text: Not measured.

frequency.text: The trial asked for at least 1 cup a day [tfood-jenkins2012].

timing.debate: No substantive published debate on timing found.

timing.summary: Nuts lowered oxidized LDL within 3 months and improved sperm quality, including DNA fragmentation, after 12-14 weeks, about one full sperm cycle. Long-term cardiovascular benefit in PREDIMED accrued over about 5 years.

onset.text: Oxidized LDL fell after 3 months on a Mediterranean diet with 30 g/day nuts [tfood-fito2007].

full.text: Sperm vitality, motility and morphology improved after 12 weeks of 75 g/day walnuts [tfood-robbins2012], and count plus DNA fragmentation after 14 weeks of 60 g/day nuts [tfood-salashuetos2018]; CVD events lower over a median 4.8 years [tfood-estruch2018].

after_stopping.text: Not measured.

frequency.text: All trials used a daily handful or more [tfood-robbins2012, tfood-salashuetos2018].

sperm.late_start: Unknown: the trials measured only at the end (12-14 weeks), so how much a 2-4 week start helps was not tested.
sperm.text: Effects were measured after 12-14 weeks, matching one spermatogenic cycle [tfood-robbins2012, tfood-salashuetos2018]. Sperm take about 64 days (range 42-76) from labelled precursor to ejaculate [tfood-misell2006], and the classic ~74-day estimate is uncertain by about a week [tfood-amann2008], so a diet change needs roughly 2.5-3 months to reach every stage of the sperm in a given ejaculate.

timing.debate: No substantive published debate on timing found.

timing.summary: DASH lowers blood pressure within a week, and most of the effect is there by then, unlike salt reduction, which keeps working for at least 4 weeks. How fast blood pressure rises again after stopping was not measured.

onset.text: Systolic BP 4.4 mmHg lower than control after 1 week [tfood-juraschek2017]; changes evident within 2 weeks in hypertensives [tfood-conlin2000].

full.text: No further fall after week 1 in DASH-Sodium [tfood-juraschek2017]; effect held through 8 weeks of feeding [tfood-appel1997].

after_stopping.text: Not measured in the feeding trials.

frequency.text: The effect comes from the current diet [tfood-juraschek2017], so it lasts only as long as the eating pattern does.

timing.debate: No substantive published debate on timing found.

timing.summary: Lipid oxidation improves within 3 months and semen quality within 4 months, while lower cardiovascular events took years. Six weeks of a Mediterranean-style supplement before IVF already changed embryo development.

onset.text: Oxidized LDL -10.6 U/L at 3 months [tfood-fito2007]; embryo cleavage changes after 6 weeks of a Mediterranean-type intervention before IVF [tfood-kermack2020].

full.text: Major CVD events lower over a median 4.8 years (HR 0.69-0.72) [tfood-estruch2018].

after_stopping.text: Not measured.

frequency.text: A whole daily eating pattern; effects in trials came from sustained adherence [tfood-estruch2018].

sperm.late_start: Unknown; the trial measured only after 4 months.
sperm.text: A 4-month Mediterranean diet plus exercise program improved sperm concentration, motility and morphology [tfood-montano2022]. Sperm take about 64 days (range 42-76) from labelled precursor to ejaculate [tfood-misell2006], and the classic ~74-day estimate is uncertain by about a week [tfood-amann2008], so a diet change needs roughly 2.5-3 months to reach every stage of the sperm in a given ejaculate.

egg.late_start: Six weeks of an omega-3, vitamin D and olive oil intervention changed embryo cleavage timing [tfood-kermack2020], so a late start may still help.
egg.text: Lower adherence before IVF was linked to lower live birth in women under 35 [tfood-karayiannis2018]. A follicle grows for several months before ovulation, including about 70 days from the preantral stage to 2 mm [tfood-gougeon2010], so anything acting on the growing follicle needs roughly 3-4 months to cover the whole final growth phase.

timing.debate: PREDIMED's timing of benefit and overall trustworthiness are disputed after its retraction and republication [tfood-agarwal2019, tfood-estruch2018].

timing.summary: Cognitive effects of diet are expected to build over years: the cohort link appeared over about 5 years of follow-up. The 3-year randomized trial found no difference against a calorie-matched control.

onset.text: No difference after 3 years in the randomized trial [tfood-barnes2023].

full.text: Cohort association over an average 4.7 years [tfood-morris2015].

after_stopping.text: Not measured.

frequency.text: A whole daily eating pattern [tfood-morris2015].

timing.debate: Cohort data suggest slower decline over 4.7 years [tfood-morris2015], but the 3-year trial was null [tfood-barnes2023]; whether 3 years was too short or the cohort link was confounded is unresolved.
